newsitem.title: UK: Several injured as gales wreak havoc in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Several injured as gales wreak havoc in Britain.

text.p: Fierce gales and heavy rain lashed Britain overnight, injuring several people and leaving thousands of homes without power, emergency services said on Tuesday.
No deaths were reported as the gales wreaked havoc with gusts of up to 145 kph (90 mph).
Fallen trees blocked a number of roads. Police and motoring organisations urged people not to travel unless it was absolutely necessary.
Rail services were badly disrupted in some areas and ferry sailings to France were delayed.
British meteorologists said the storms stemmed from Hurricane Lili which caused widespread damage in Cuba and the Bahamas just over a week ago.
Thousands of people in southern England and Wales were left in darkness after power cables were pulled down.
In Pembrokeshire in west Wales, fire fighters were called in to pump out flooded properties and to make damaged roofs safe.
An unmanned exploratory oil platform was ripped from its moorings in Portland harbour on England's south coast and hit rocks. A tug was sent to secure it.
Several major road bridges were closed to traffic. A smaller one over the river Wey, south of London, collapsed into the water.
In the southern English town of Warminster, drivers were confused after the gales blew traffic lights round the wrong way.
